sentences.zh: 他现在建立了一个令人难以置信的政治组织，他将其戏称为“军事机器”。

sentences.en: Every Indiana Claven, Klan Lodge, will draw up data on every candidate for political office in the state of Indiana, and the Klan will sift through them all.
sentences.zh: 印第安纳州的每一个克莱文（Claven）和三K党分会，都会搜集印第安纳州每一位政治公职候选人的资料，然后由三K党进行筛选。

sentences.en: And the data includes every opinion these people have ever expressed, their schools, their kids go to,
sentences.zh: 这些资料包括这些人曾经表达过的每一个观点、他们上过的学校、他们孩子就读的学校，

sentences.en: their ethnic background, all of these kinds of things, what clubs they've joined.
sentences.zh: 他们的种族背景，诸如此类的事情，以及他们加入过什么俱乐部。

sentences.en: Then the Klan makes its choice.
sentences.zh: 然后，三K党做出选择。

sentences.en: The Klan will then campaign for these people.
sentences.zh: 接着，三K党会为这些人开展竞选活动。

sentences.en: They will get
sentences.zh: 他们会找来

sentences.en: Protestant ministers to talk about them in their sermons.
sentences.zh: 新教牧师在布道时谈论这些候选人。

sentences.en: They will publish the approved slate in
sentences.zh: 他们会在主日学校的通讯中

sentences.en: Sunday school newsletters.
sentences.zh: 公布获批的候选人名单。

sentences.en: Klansmen will leave a special copy of the Fiery Cross telling you how to vote on your porch on election day.
sentences.zh: 选举日当天，三K党成员会把一份特别版的《火十字报》放在你的门廊上，告诉你该怎么投票。

sentences.en: They have hundreds of cars ready to take Protestant voters to the polls.
sentences.zh: 他们准备了数百辆汽车，专门负责接送新教选民去投票站。

sentences.en: Klan's women will stand ready to mind people's children so women can go and vote.
sentences.zh: 三K党的妇女成员则随时待命，帮人照看孩子，好让妇女们能去投票。

sentences.en: All of this.
sentences.zh: 所有这些。

sentences.en: And it's a brilliant success.
sentences.zh: 而且这取得了辉煌的成功。

sentences.en: It is an object lesson in how political organization in kind of local America works.
sentences.zh: 这堪称美国地方政治组织运作方式的一个典型案例。

sentences.en: Because in 1924, almost every single Klan candidate in Indiana is elected to office, going all the way from mayors and district attorneys to sheriffs and school boards.
sentences.zh: 因为在1924年，印第安纳州几乎每一位三K党候选人都当选了公职，从市长、地区检察官到警长和学校董事会成员，无一例外。

sentences.en: And Stevenson thinks to himself, well, if I can do this in Indiana, I can do this anywhere.
sentences.zh: 史蒂文森心想，好吧，如果我在印第安纳能做到这一点，我就能在任何地方做到。

sentences.en: So in his headquarters in Indianapolis, he has a bust of Napoleon.
sentences.zh: 所以，在印第安纳波利斯的总部里，他摆放了一尊拿破仑的半身像。

sentences.en: He has eight phones,
sentences.zh: 他有八部电话，

sentences.en: including one of them, which he claims is a direct line to the White House, but no one is ever allowed to lift it because it's obviously just a complete fake.
sentences.zh: 其中一部他声称是直通白宫的专线，但从来没人被允许接听，因为那显然完全是个骗局。

sentences.en: And he says to his aides,
sentences.zh: 他对手下说：

sentences.en: I'm a nobody from nowhere, but I've got the biggest brains and I'm going to be the biggest man in the
sentences.zh: “我是一个来自无名之地的无名小卒，但我拥有最聪明的大脑，我将成为美国最了不起的人。”

sentences.en: United States.
sentences.zh: 美国。

sentences.en: And the first step to this is basically seizing control of the National Klan from the dentiSt. So in the summer of 1924, he declares independence from the National Klan
sentences.zh: 而实现这一目标的第一步，基本上就是从那个牙医手中夺取全国三K党的控制权。因此，在1924年夏天，他宣布脱离全国三K党，

sentences.en: and he triggers this Klan civil war.
sentences.zh: 并引发了这场三K党内战。

sentences.en: So it's basically Indiana is leading a revolt against
sentences.zh: 所以基本上是印第安纳州在领导一场针对

sentences.en: Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 亚特兰大的反叛。

sentences.en: There's a huge and very bizarre and Baroque struggle for power in which they're sort of suing each other for libel.
sentences.zh: 这是一场规模宏大、极其怪异且荒诞的权力斗争，他们甚至互相起诉对方诽谤。

sentences.en: Stevenson's local lodge is persuaded to kick him out.
sentences.zh: 史蒂文森当地的分会被说服将他开除。

sentences.en: He accuses Hiram Evans of blowing up his yacht.
sentences.zh: 他指控海勒姆·埃文斯炸毁了他的游艇。

sentences.en: I'm not sure how true that is.
sentences.zh: 我不确定这事有几分真实性。

sentences.en: And this struggle in summer of 1924 seems perfectly poised.
sentences.zh: 而这场1924年夏天的斗争似乎正处于胶着状态。

sentences.en: So let's just pause that here because we're in the middle of 1924 and don't forget the Klan is going to try and get involved in national politics and play the part of Kingmaker.
sentences.zh: 那么我们先暂停一下，因为我们正处于1924年的中期，别忘了三K党正试图介入全国政治，扮演“造王者”的角色。

sentences.en: Now the Klan has already been very successful.
sentences.zh: 现在，三K党已经非常成功了。

sentences.en: They've elected a senator from Texas.
sentences.zh: 他们选出了一位来自德克萨斯州的参议员。

sentences.en: They've won all sorts of public offices and states as diverse as we talked last time as Oregon and the Northwestern, Texas, right down by the Mexican border.
sentences.zh: 他们赢得了各种公职，在像我们上次提到的俄勒冈州和西北部，以及靠近墨西哥边境的德克萨斯州等各不相同的州都取得了胜利。

sentences.en: They have probably got about
sentences.zh: 他们可能已经拥有了大约

sentences.en: 16 senators in the US Senate loyal to the Klan and about 75 congressmen in the House of Representatives and probably 11 governors.
sentences.zh: 16名忠于三K党的美国参议员，众议院里大约有75名国会议员，可能还有11位州长。

sentences.en: Again, loyal to the Klan.
sentences.zh: 同样，都是忠于三K党的。

sentences.en: These are Linda Gordon's figures.
sentences.zh: 这些是琳达·戈登的数据。

sentences.en: But what they really want to do is to play a part in the presidential election.
sentences.zh: 但他们真正想做的是在总统选举中发挥作用。

sentences.en: So the Republican candidate in the presidential election is Calvin Coolidge.
sentences.zh: 共和党的总统候选人是卡尔文·柯立芝。

sentences.en: He in some ways would be a suitable candidate for the Klan.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，他本应是三K党合适的候选人。

sentences.en: He's of Protestant stock going back to the Puritans in the 17th century.
sentences.zh: 他的新教血统可以追溯到17世纪的清教徒。

sentences.en: He's very clean living, all of this.
sentences.zh: 他生活非常检点，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But Coolidge hates the Klan.
sentences.zh: 但柯立芝讨厌三K党。

sentences.en: He never made a public statement about them, but he is known to dislike them.
sentences.zh: 他从未就他们发表过公开声明，但众所周知他很反感他们。

sentences.en: He never knowingly appoints the Klansmen to public office.
sentences.zh: 他从不故意任命三K党成员担任公职。

sentences.en: And Coolidge supports black civil rights.
sentences.zh: 而且柯立芝支持黑人民权。

sentences.en: And he goes out of his way to praise the contribution that immigrants have made to American life.
sentences.zh: 他还不遗余力地赞扬移民对美国生活所做的贡献。

sentences.en: So he thinks basically the Ku Klux Klan are evil.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上认为三K党是邪恶的。

sentences.en: Yeah, he thinks they're a total scum.
sentences.zh: 是的，他认为他们是一群彻头彻尾的渣滓。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the Klan then turn their attention to the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 于是三K党将注意力转向了民主党。

sentences.en: And they all go en masse to the
sentences.zh: 他们集体前往

sentences.en: Democratic convention at Madison Square Garden in New York.
sentences.zh: 纽约麦迪逊广场花园参加民主党全国代表大会。

sentences.en: Hiram Evans, the dentist, leads the Klan leadership.
sentences.zh: 牙医海勒姆·埃文斯领导着三K党的高层。

sentences.en: And they know who they want to be, the Democratic candidates.
sentences.zh: 他们知道自己想要谁成为民主党的候选人。

sentences.en: And he's actually the favorite.
sentences.zh: 而且他实际上还是热门人选。

sentences.en: He is the son-in-law of Woodrow Wilson, who had praised the birth of a nation.
sentences.zh: 他是伍德罗·威尔逊的女婿，而威尔逊曾称赞过《一个国家的诞生》这部电影。

sentences.en: This is a man called William Gibbs McAdoo.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫威廉·吉布斯·麦卡杜。

sentences.en: And McAdoo is the former US Treasury Secretary.
sentences.zh: 麦卡杜是前美国财政部长。

sentences.en: McAdoo is a huge fan of prohibition.
sentences.zh: 麦卡杜是禁酒令的忠实拥护者。

sentences.en: He is the candidate, the champion of rural Protestant America.
sentences.zh: 他是农村新教美国人的候选人，是他们的捍卫者。

sentences.en: And standing against him for the Democratic nomination is the Klan's worst enemy, their worst nightmare.
sentences.zh: 而与他竞争民主党提名的是三K党最大的敌人，他们最可怕的噩梦。

sentences.en: Al Smith, the governor of New York, a Catholic.
sentences.zh: 阿尔·史密斯，纽约州州长，一位天主教徒。

sentences.en: Oh my God, the horror.
sentences.zh: 天哪，太可怕了。

sentences.en: And the convention, it's the longest convention nominating process in American history.
sentences.zh: 这次大会是美国历史上最漫长的提名过程。

sentences.en: It took 103 ballots, 103 rounds of voting to get a winner.
sentences.zh: 它进行了103轮投票才选出获胜者。

sentences.en: To the Klan's delight, Al Smith does not win.
sentences.zh: 令三K党高兴的是，阿尔·史密斯没有赢。

sentences.en: But to their horror, William Gibbs McAdoo doesn't win either.
sentences.zh: 但令他们恐惧的是，威廉·吉布斯·麦卡杜也没有赢。

sentences.en: The convention compromises on the former ambassador to Great Britain, who's called John W.
sentences.zh: 大会最终折中选择了前驻英国大使，名叫约翰·W·

sentences.en: Davis.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯。

sentences.en: No one needs to worry about him.
sentences.zh: 没人需要担心他。

sentences.en: He's completely forgotten.
sentences.zh: 他已经被彻底遗忘了。

sentences.en: And what's worse for the Klan is there's then a massive row about the Klan itself.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，随后还爆发了一场关于三K党本身的激烈争吵。

sentences.en: Basically, the anti-McAdoo people, the delegates, introduced a resolution to condemn the Klan.
sentences.zh: 基本上，反麦卡杜派的代表们提出了一项谴责三K党的决议。

sentences.en: And it almost passed.
sentences.zh: 而且它差点就通过了。

sentences.en: It lost by four votes out of more than 1,000 votes.
sentences.zh: 它以四票之差在超过1000张选票中落败。

sentences.en: And for the Klan, this is a terrible shock.
sentences.zh: 对于三K党来说，这是一个可怕的打击。

sentences.en: That actually, they're not as influential in importance as they thought.
sentences.zh: 因为他们实际上并没有自己想象中那么有影响力。

sentences.en: So they're not kingmakers at all?
sentences.zh: 所以他们根本不是什么造王者？

sentences.en: They're not kingmakers after all.
sentences.zh: 毕竟他们不是造王者。

sentences.en: And as the convention breaks up and we go to the national election, which Coolidge ends up winning, the Klan look at their membership roles and their
sentences.zh: 随着大会闭幕，我们进入了全国大选，最终柯立芝获胜，三K党查看他们的会员名册，发现他们的

sentences.en: membership roles are beginning to fall, shockingly.
sentences.zh: 会员人数开始惊人地下降。

sentences.en: Because all the infighting means that a lot of ordinary Klansmen have kind of lost confidence in the organization.
sentences.zh: 因为所有的内斗意味着许多普通三K党成员对该组织失去了信心。

sentences.en: You know, they're all squabbling among themselves.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们都在互相争吵。

sentences.en: They all look like they're really corrupt.
sentences.zh: 他们看起来都非常腐败。

sentences.en: There's so many revelations of bad behavior.
sentences.zh: 有太多关于不良行为的揭露了。

sentences.en: Then when the people go to the poll, the American people go to the polls in November
sentences.zh: 然后当人们去投票时，美国人民在11月去投票时

sentences.en: 1924 in Texas, which had been the, you know, it's been the great state where the Klan had made their breakthrough.
sentences.zh: 1924年的德克萨斯州，那曾是三K党取得突破的伟大州，

sentences.en: They'd got the senator in and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 他们选出了参议员等等。

sentences.en: There is a backlash against the Klan.
sentences.zh: 那里出现了针对三K党的强烈抵制。

sentences.en: Their candidate for governor, their total disbelief ends up losing.
sentences.zh: 他们的州长候选人，在他们完全不敢置信的情况下落选了。

sentences.en: Anti-Klan candidates are elected across the board.
sentences.zh: 反三K党候选人全面当选。

sentences.en: The new Texas legislature passed a law against wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州新立法机构通过了一项禁止戴面具的法律。

sentences.en: Klansmen are stripped of their public offices.
sentences.zh: 三K党成员被剥夺了公职。

sentences.en: They're driven out of the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 他们被赶出了民主党。

sentences.en: And suddenly membership of the
sentences.zh: 突然间，三K党的会员人数

sentences.en: Klan just drops off a cliff in Texas.
sentences.zh: 在德克萨斯州直线下降。

sentences.en: So by 1926, the Klan lodges in Dallas, Houston, San Antonio, and Fort Worth, which had been very, very popular, some of the most successful in the country,
sentences.zh: 所以到了1926年，达拉斯、休斯顿、圣安东尼奥和沃斯堡的三K党分会，这些曾经非常非常受欢迎、全国最成功的分会，

sentences.en: have fallen so far they're in the hands of receivers.
sentences.zh: 已经衰落到被接管的地步。

sentences.en: And membership in Dallas, a boom city for the Klan in the early 20s, is down in just a couple of years from 13,000 people to barely 1,000 people.
sentences.zh: 在20年代初曾是三K党繁荣之地的达拉斯，会员人数在短短几年内从13000人下降到勉强1000人。

sentences.en: So the Klan seems to be imploding.
sentences.zh: 所以三K党似乎正在崩溃。

sentences.en: And then we get the scandal.
sentences.zh: 然后我们迎来了这起丑闻。

sentences.en: So this is the story of Madge Oberholzer, which is, I have to warn listeners, it is a pretty grim story.
sentences.zh: 这就是玛奇·奥伯霍尔泽的故事，我必须提醒听众，这是一个相当残酷的故事。

sentences.en: So prepare yourselves.
sentences.zh: 所以请做好心理准备。

sentences.en: Madge Oberholzer enters the story of the Klan on the 12th of January, 1925.
sentences.zh: 玛奇·奥伯霍尔泽于1925年1月12日进入了三K党的故事中。

sentences.en: She went to a party for the inauguration of the new Indiana governor, Ed Jackson, who was widely seen as the Klan's puppet.
sentences.zh: 她去参加了新任印第安纳州州长埃德·杰克逊的就职典礼派对，杰克逊被广泛认为是三K党的傀儡。

sentences.en: And at this party, she met David C.
sentences.zh: 在这个派对上，她遇到了大卫·C·

sentences.en: Stevenson, the, what is it, the Grand Dragon.
sentences.zh: 史蒂文森，那个什么，大龙（Grand Dragon）。

sentences.en: And what is Madge like?
sentences.zh: 玛奇是个什么样的人？

sentences.en: So Madge is 28 years old.
sentences.zh: 玛奇今年28岁。

sentences.en: She's very shy.
sentences.zh: 她非常害羞。

sentences.en: She's not an especially socially dazzling person.
sentences.zh: 她并不是一个特别善于社交的人。

sentences.en: She lives with her parents, Methodists.
sentences.zh: 她和父母住在一起，是卫理公会教徒。

sentences.en: She runs the Indiana Young People's Reading Circle.
sentences.zh: 她负责印第安纳青年阅读圈的工作。

sentences.en: So they start dating.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始约会。

sentences.en: They go, they dance and they start dating.
sentences.zh: 他们一起跳舞，开始约会。

sentences.en: On the 15th of March, Stevenson's secretary rang her parents' home.
sentences.zh: 3月15日，史蒂文森的秘书给她的父母家打了电话。

sentences.en: And she said, the Grand Dragon needs to see Madge at once.
sentences.zh: 她说，大龙需要立刻见玛奇。

sentences.en: So she changed into her best black dress and his bodyguard picked her up and drove off with her into the night.
sentences.zh: 于是她换上了她最好的黑色连衣裙，他的保镖接上她，带着她驶入了夜色中。

sentences.en: And she arrived at Stevenson's house to find him incredibly drunk.
sentences.zh: 她到达史蒂文森家时，发现他醉得一塌糊涂。

sentences.en: And he and his men then forced her to drink loads of whiskey until she was sick.
sentences.zh: 他和他的手下强迫她喝了大量的威士忌，直到她呕吐不止。

sentences.en: And then they hustled her into a car and took her off to Union Station, Indianapolis.
sentences.zh: 然后他们把她塞进车里，带到了印第安纳波利斯的联合车站。

sentences.en: And they put her onto the train to Chicago with Stevenson in Stevenson's private compartment.
sentences.zh: 他们把她送上了去芝加哥的火车，史蒂文森也在史蒂文森的私人包厢里。

sentences.en: And she presumably is a virginal, God-fearing, upstanding spinster.
sentences.zh: 她大概是一个纯洁、敬畏上帝、正直的老姑娘。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's exactly what she is.
sentences.zh: 她就是那样的人。

sentences.en: Methodist home, lives with her parents, likes reading, all of that.
sentences.zh: 卫理公会家庭，和父母住在一起，喜欢阅读，诸如此类。

sentences.en: The train sets off.
sentences.zh: 火车出发了。

sentences.en: And once the train sets off, she is now absolutely slaughtered because they forced her to drink all this whiskey.
sentences.zh: 火车一开动，她就彻底烂醉如泥了，因为他们强迫她喝了那么多威士忌。

sentences.en: And he repeatedly rapes her.
sentences.zh: 他反复强奸了她。

sentences.en: She's so drunk that she can't resiSt. And what is more, he bites her all over her body.
sentences.zh: 她醉得无法反抗。而且更过分的是，他在她全身各处咬她。

sentences.en: So very deep bites.
sentences.zh: 咬得很深。

sentences.en: I mean, these are not, you know, these are serious bites.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这些不是，你知道，这些是严重的咬伤。

sentences.en: Like he has literally said afterwards, like he was literally trying to chew her.
sentences.zh: 就像他事后说的，他简直是在试图咀嚼她。

sentences.en: So from the, from her kind of from her head all the way down to her feet, they reach the town of Hammond, which is just outside
sentences.zh: 从她的头部一直到脚部，他们到达了哈蒙德镇，就在芝加哥郊外，

sentences.en: Chicago, just on the Indiana side of the state boundary.
sentences.zh: 正好在州界的印第安纳州一侧。

sentences.en: And they get out there and check into her hotel.
sentences.zh: 他们在那儿下车，住进了一家酒店。

sentences.en: She's sort of being carried by his bodyguards.
sentences.zh: 她几乎是被他的保镖抬进去的。

sentences.en: At one point, she says to Stevenson,
sentences.zh: 有一次，她对史蒂文森说：

sentences.en: I'm going to set the law on you.
sentences.zh: “我要动用法律来制裁你。”

sentences.en: And he says to her, I am the law in Indiana.
sentences.zh: 他对她说：“在印第安纳，我就是法律。”

sentences.en: They go up to the room.
sentences.zh: 他们回到房间。

sentences.en: He falls asleep.
sentences.zh: 他睡着了。

sentences.en: She persuades his chauffeur to take her out to a drug store.
sentences.zh: 她说服了他的司机带她去药店。

sentences.en: And there she buys some mercury bichloride tablets, which were used then to treat syphilis.
sentences.zh: 她在那里买了一些氯化汞药片，当时这种药被用来治疗梅毒。

sentences.en: She wanted to kill herself.
sentences.zh: 她想自杀。

sentences.en: She was so horrified and ashamed about what had happened to her.
sentences.zh: 她对自己遭遇的一切感到无比恐惧和羞愧。

sentences.en: She takes three of the tablets.
sentences.zh: 她服下了三片药。

sentences.en: She intended to take the lot, but she could only swallow three and immediately became horribly ill and started vomiting blood everywhere.
sentences.zh: 她本想把剩下的全吃了，但只吞下三片就立刻病得极其严重，开始到处呕吐鲜血。

sentences.en: Stevenson has now woken up from his drunken stupor and he panics.
sentences.zh: 史蒂文森此时从醉酒的昏迷中醒来，陷入了恐慌。

sentences.en: And he says to his bodyguards, drive us back towards Indianapolis.
sentences.zh: 他告诉保镖，开车送我们回印第安纳波利斯。

sentences.en: In the car, she's in a terrible state, poor mad.
sentences.zh: 在车里，她处于一种极其糟糕的状态，可怜的玛奇。

sentences.en: She's been sick all over the car.
sentences.zh: 她吐得车里到处都是。

sentences.en: Stevenson keeps saying to her, you must forget this.
sentences.zh: 史蒂文森不停地对她说，你必须忘了这件事。

sentences.en: What's done is done.
sentences.zh: 事已至此，无可挽回。

sentences.en: I am the law.
sentences.zh: 我就是法律。

sentences.en: I am the power.
sentences.zh: 我就是权力。

sentences.en: But clearly he's anxious because he keeps saying to her, we should stop and you should marry me.
sentences.zh: 但显然他很焦虑，因为他一直在对她说，我们应该停下来，你应该嫁给我。

sentences.en: You know, because basically he wants to shut her up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，因为他基本上是想让她闭嘴。

sentences.en: And she says, I won't marry you and all this.
sentences.zh: 她说，我不会嫁给你，诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: And eventually after a long delay, they take her home and they say to her parents who are horrified by the sight of her, oh, we've been in a car accident.
sentences.zh: 最终在长时间的耽搁后，他们把她送回了家，并对看到她惨状而惊恐万分的父母谎称，哦，我们出了车祸。

sentences.en: Her parents are not fooled by this.
sentences.zh: 她的父母并没有被骗过。

sentences.en: And poor Madge, she lived for another month in terrible agony.
sentences.zh: 可怜的玛奇，她在极度的痛苦中又活了一个月。

sentences.en: And she died on the 14th of April of infection from the bites, as well as kidney failure from the mercury poisoning.
sentences.zh: 她在4月14日去世，死因是咬伤引发的感染，以及汞中毒导致的肾衰竭。

sentences.en: And by this point, her father had already gone to the police.
sentences.zh: 而此时，她的父亲已经报了警。

sentences.en: And Stevenson was charged with rape, kidnapping, assault and battery, and second degree murder.
sentences.zh: 史蒂文森被控强奸、绑架、殴打和二级谋杀。

sentences.en: Murder because doctors testified in courts that the infected bites alone would have been enough to kill her.
sentences.zh: 之所以控告谋杀，是因为医生在法庭上作证说，仅凭那些感染的咬伤就足以致她于死地。

sentences.en: So it didn't require the mercury poisoning as well.
sentences.zh: 所以并不一定非要汞中毒才行。

sentences.en: Stevenson was convinced that his connections in Indiana meant that he would get off.
sentences.zh: 史蒂文森坚信他在印第安纳州的人脉能让他脱罪。

sentences.en: He couldn't believe it when in November
1925, he was found guilty and sentenced to life in prison and sent to the Michigan City Penitentiary.
sentences.zh: 他被判有罪并被判处终身监禁，送往密歇根市监狱时，他简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: And he believed that the governor, his puppet, Governor Jackson, would pardon him.
sentences.zh: 他曾以为他的傀儡——州长杰克逊会赦免他。

sentences.en: But no pardon came.
sentences.zh: 但赦免并没有到来。

sentences.en: And eventually Stevenson loses patience and he gives all of his confidential papers to the Indianapolis
sentences.zh: 最终史蒂文森失去了耐心，他把所有机密文件都交给了《印第安纳波利斯

sentences.en: Times.
sentences.zh: 时报》。

sentences.en: And he says to them, well, I'll tell you all about the bribes that I've paid to local officials.
sentences.zh: 他告诉他们，好吧，我会把贿赂当地官员的所有细节都告诉你们。

sentences.en: And the result was an earthquake in Indiana politics.
sentences.zh: 结果引发了印第安纳州政坛的一场大地震。

sentences.en: Up to this point, very heavily
sentences.zh: 在此之前，这里非常

sentences.en: Republican.
sentences.zh: 倾向共和党。

sentences.en: The scandal took down the governor of Indiana, the mayor of Indianapolis, the local head of the Republican Party, loads of state officials, loads of mayors, all of this kind of
sentences.zh: 这起丑闻拉下了印第安纳州州长、印第安纳波利斯市长、共和党当地负责人、大批州政府官员、大批市长，所有这类

sentences.en: thing.
sentences.zh: 人。

sentences.en: And so it is that by the end of the decade, the Democrats had won pretty much every city in the state.
sentences.zh: 因此，到十年结束时，民主党几乎赢得了该州所有的城市。

sentences.en: And a disaster not just for the Republicans, but for the local clan.
sentences.zh: 这对共和党人来说是一场灾难，对当地三K党来说也是如此。

sentences.en: Once the strongest in the nation.
sentences.zh: 它曾是全国最强大的组织。

sentences.en: But the Stevenson scandal, the death of this poor woman, Madge Oberholzer, totally destroys the clan's image.
sentences.zh: 但史蒂文森丑闻，以及这位可怜的女性玛奇·奥伯霍尔泽的死，彻底摧毁了三K党的形象。

sentences.en: So in two years, its Indiana membership collapsed from hundreds and hundreds of thousands of people to just 4,000 people.
sentences.zh: 因此在两年内，其印第安纳州的成员人数从几十万之众骤减至仅剩4000人。

sentences.en: And what happens to David Stevenson?
sentences.zh: 大卫·史蒂文森后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: He was released, I think, in 1950, if I recall correctly.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，他大概是在1950年获释的。

sentences.en: He then got out.
sentences.zh: 他出狱了。

sentences.en: He then was arrested again, convicted again for sexually assaulting a 16-year-old girl, I think.
sentences.zh: 后来他又被捕了，好像是因为性侵一名16岁女孩再次被定罪。

sentences.en: So in and out of prison and then died, I think, in the 60s.
sentences.zh: 所以他进进出出监狱，最后大概是在60年代去世的。

sentences.en: And the woman he was living with, possibly his wife, I can't remember, said, oh, he seems such a nice person.
sentences.zh: 和他住在一起的女人，可能是他妻子，我不记得了，她说，哦，他看起来是个很好的人。

sentences.en: I can't believe all these stories about him are true.
sentences.zh: 我不敢相信关于他的那些传言都是真的。

sentences.en: But clearly, an incredibly dodgy and unpleasant man.
sentences.zh: 但显然，他是一个极其狡猾且令人厌恶的人。

sentences.en: Died in 1966, age 74.
sentences.zh: 1966年去世，享年74岁。

sentences.en: So what happened to the clan in Indiana was a symptom of a wider story.
sentences.zh: 所以印第安纳州三K党的遭遇是一个更广泛故事的缩影。

sentences.en: In the mid to late
sentences.zh: 在20世纪20年代

sentences.en: 1920s, the clan absolutely hemorrhaged members.
sentences.zh: 中后期，三K党的成员大量流失。

sentences.en: It had risen so quickly, and then suddenly it declines.
sentences.zh: 它崛起得如此之快，然后又突然衰落。

sentences.en: And historians have spent huge quantities of ink trying to explain why this is.
sentences.zh: 历史学家们花费了大量笔墨试图解释其中的原因。

sentences.en: There are obvious underlying reasons, as well as the scandals.
sentences.zh: 除了丑闻之外，还有明显的根本原因。

sentences.en: The clan's vision was much too negative.
sentences.zh: 三K党的愿景太消极了。

sentences.en: It had nothing positive to it.
sentences.zh: 它没有任何积极的东西。

sentences.en: It was all about hatred of Catholics and stuff more than anything else.
sentences.zh: 它主要就是关于对天主教徒等的仇恨。

sentences.en: Apart from some anodyne stuff about patriotism and family values, most of its appeal is based on negativity.
sentences.zh: 除了关于爱国主义和家庭价值观的一些平淡言论外，它的大部分吸引力都建立在消极情绪之上。

sentences.en: Its vision of America is an outdated one.
sentences.zh: 它对美国的愿景已经过时了。

sentences.en: You know, America by the 1920s is clearly much too diverse to be turned back into a white Protestant enclave.
sentences.zh: 你知道，到20世纪20年代，美国显然已经太多元化了，不可能再变回一个白人新教徒的聚居地。

sentences.en: That's never going to happen.
sentences.zh: 那是不可能发生的。

sentences.en: Also, I think most historians think it was a terrible mistake for the clan to enter mainstream politics.
sentences.zh: 此外，我认为大多数历史学家认为三K党进入主流政治是一个严重的错误。

sentences.en: The clan's values of secrecy and exclusivity don't work in a democratic arena where you have to make deals and compromises.
sentences.zh: 三K党的秘密和排他性价值观在民主舞台上行不通，因为那里需要达成交易和妥协。

sentences.en: And you have to, you know, a pluralistic world in which you're appealing to bigotry and sectarianism, it doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 而且你必须面对一个多元化的世界，在这种世界里，诉诸偏执和宗派主义是行不通的。

sentences.en: There are some historians like Linda Gordon who point out that actually maybe the clan stopped being so popular because it had actually won some of its battles.
sentences.zh: 有一些历史学家，比如琳达·戈登，指出三K党之所以不再那么受欢迎，实际上可能是因为它已经赢得了一些斗争。

sentences.en: So the clan was always in favour of eugenics.
sentences.zh: 三K党一直支持优生学。

sentences.en: And by the end of the 1920s, 30 American states had adopted eugenics laws with forced sterilisation of criminals or people that were called defectives.
sentences.zh: 到20世纪20年代末，30个美国州通过了优生学法律，对罪犯或所谓的“缺陷者”进行强制绝育。

sentences.en: And often the people who were singled out for this treatment tended to be very poor people or black people.
sentences.zh: 而且被选中接受这种待遇的人往往是非常贫穷的人或黑人。

sentences.en: So in other words, people that the clan didn't really like anyway.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就是三K党本来就不喜欢的人。

sentences.en: The clan also won the argument on immigration.
sentences.zh: 三K党还在移民问题上赢得了辩论。

sentences.en: So in 1924, the Johnson-Reed Act brought in immigration quotas that were based on an outdated census, the 1890 census.
sentences.zh: 因此在1924年，《约翰逊-里德法案》引入了基于过时人口普查（1890年人口普查）的移民配额。

sentences.en: So basically an immigration regime that tried to turn about the clock because 70% of immigrants under this new legislation had to come from Britain, Germany, or Ireland.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上这是一个试图倒转时钟的移民制度，因为根据这项新立法，70%的移民必须来自英国、德国或爱尔兰。

sentences.en: So in other words, let's try to recreate a 19th century white
sentences.zh: 换句话说，让我们试着重建一个19世纪的白人

sentences.en: America.
sentences.zh: 美国。

sentences.en: All immigration from Asia, for example, was banned under the new legislation.
sentences.zh: 例如，根据新立法，所有来自亚洲的移民都被禁止。

sentences.en: And Southern and
sentences.zh: 而来自南欧和

sentences.en: Eastern European immigration was severely curtailed.
sentences.zh: 东欧的移民受到了严格限制。

sentences.en: And this regime lasted until the 50s.
sentences.zh: 这种制度一直持续到50年代。

sentences.en: And partly as a result of this, anti-Catholicism as a force in American life basically began to dissipate.
sentences.zh: 作为结果之一，作为美国生活中一股力量的反天主教情绪基本上开始消散。

sentences.en: So, you know, the Pope's plot to attack the people of North Manchester on the northbound train.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，教皇袭击北曼彻斯特北行火车乘客的阴谋。

sentences.en: By disguising himself as a corset salesman.
sentences.zh: 通过伪装成紧身胸衣推销员。

sentences.en: Yeah, that never comes to fruition.
sentences.zh: 是的，那从未实现。

sentences.en: You know, the clan has been saying for years, the Pope is poised to launch his attack.
sentences.zh: 你知道，三K党多年来一直说，教皇准备发动袭击。

sentences.en: But the Pope never does.
sentences.zh: 但教皇从未这样做。

sentences.en: The uprising of armed Catholics never happens.
sentences.zh: 武装天主教徒的起义从未发生。

sentences.en: And so people start, I think, over time to say to themselves, this is obviously demented.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为随着时间的推移，人们开始对自己说，这显然是疯了。

sentences.en: You know, this is never going to happen.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这永远不会发生。

sentences.en: And the clan just starts to sound a bit silly.
sentences.zh: 三K党开始听起来有点愚蠢了。

sentences.en: The other thing, of course, is the clan's violence.
sentences.zh: 当然，另一件事是三K党的暴力行为。

sentences.en: Things like the killings in Mare Rouge that we talked about, the reign of terror in Goose Creek, the murder of Madge Oberholzer, the vigilante violence in Williamson County.
sentences.zh: 比如我们谈到的红马镇杀戮、鹅溪的恐怖统治、玛奇·奥伯霍尔泽的谋杀案、威廉姆森县的治安维持会暴力事件。

sentences.en: To most of the people who are there for the picnic and the barbecues, they're not up for all this.
sentences.zh: 对于大多数去参加野餐和烧烤的人来说，他们并不想参与这些。

sentences.en: They're horrified by all this, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们对这一切感到恐惧。

sentences.en: And so once that becomes established in the public mind, people say, listen, I don't want to have anything to do with this organisation after all.
sentences.zh: 一旦这一点在公众心中确立，人们就会说，听着，我不想再和这个组织有任何瓜葛了。

sentences.en: So by the late 1920s, the numbers are in freefall.
sentences.zh: 所以到了20世纪20年代末，人数呈自由落体式下降。

sentences.en: They've collapsed.
sentences.zh: 他们崩溃了。

sentences.en: And then the depression strikes.
sentences.zh: 然后大萧条来袭。

sentences.en: No one's got any money.
sentences.zh: 没人有钱了。

sentences.en: You're not going to spend your money on cleck tokens and ludicrous garb if you haven't got any money.
sentences.zh: 如果你没钱，你不会把钱花在三K党的徽章和荒谬的服装上。

sentences.en: The clan completely loses its mojo in the 30s.
sentences.zh: 三K党在30年代彻底失去了魔力。

sentences.en: Hiram Evans, the dentist, is still running the clan, and he tries to rebrand it.
sentences.zh: 牙医海勒姆·埃文斯仍在经营三K党，他试图重塑品牌。

sentences.en: He actually abandons the anti-Catholicism and says, we're an anti-communist group.
sentences.zh: 他实际上放弃了反天主教，说我们是一个反共组织。

sentences.zh: 我们反对工会。

sentences.en: That's what we're all about.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的宗旨。

sentences.en: But basically, no one's really interested.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，没人真的感兴趣。

sentences.en: He ended up resigning in 1939 as imperial wizard.
sentences.zh: 他最终在1939年辞去了帝国巫师的职务。

sentences.en: They'd done him no good at all.
sentences.zh: 这对他一点好处都没有。

sentences.en: The clan just splintered and splintered, and then it disbanded in a very banal way for tax reasons.
sentences.zh: 三K党只是不断分裂，最后因为税务原因以一种非常平庸的方式解散了。

sentences.en: Now, of course, that's not the end of the clan or a clan as a feature of American life.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并不是三K党作为美国生活特征的终结。

sentences.en: So there is a third clan.
sentences.zh: 所以还有第三个三K党。

sentences.en: And this was founded in 1946 at the same place as the second clan, Stone Mountain, Georgia.
sentences.zh: 它成立于1946年，地点与第二个三K党相同，即佐治亚州的石山。

sentences.en: This is the one that still exists.
sentences.zh: 这就是至今仍然存在的那个。

sentences.en: So this basically is anti-communist and intensely raciSt. It's well known because it carries out some hideous atrocities.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上是反共且极度种族主义的。它之所以出名，是因为它实施了一些骇人听闻的暴行。

sentences.en: So bombing of black churches in Birmingham, Alabama, and killing civil rights workers in 1963 and 1964.
sentences.zh: 比如1963年和1964年炸毁阿拉巴马州伯明翰的黑人教堂，杀害民权工作者。

sentences.en: Some very famous examples.
sentences.zh: 一些非常著名的例子。

sentences.en: But it doesn't have many members.
sentences.zh: 但它的成员并不多。

sentences.en: It's purely reactionary and raciSt. Insofar as it thrives at all, it's in counterpoint to the civil rights movement, which is obviously much bigger than the clan is.
sentences.zh: 它纯粹是反动和种族主义的。它之所以能存活，是因为它与民权运动形成了对比，而民权运动显然比三K党大得多。

sentences.en: It's never remotely a mass movement.
sentences.zh: 它从来都不是一个群众运动。

sentences.en: It still exists today, but it has, I think, fewer than 3,000 members, according to researchers.
sentences.zh: 它今天仍然存在，但据研究人员称，它只有不到3000名成员。

sentences.en: Was it David Duke?
sentences.zh: 是大卫·杜克吗？

sentences.en: See, David Duke, everyone's heard of David Duke, but he was never a significant.
sentences.zh: 你看，大卫·杜克，每个人都听说过大卫·杜克，但他从来都不是一个重要人物。

sentences.en: It's his exoticism, I think, that makes him interesting.
sentences.zh: 我认为正是他的异国情调让他变得有趣。

sentences.en: He's the kind of character that Louis Theroux depends on for his TV prograMs. Kind of sinister, but not so sinister that he wouldn't look ridiculous if he comes on a TV show.
sentences.zh: 他是路易·泰鲁在电视节目中依赖的那种角色。有点阴险，但又不至于阴险到上电视节目时看起来很荒谬。

sentences.zh: 我认为第二个三K党是这几个组织中最有趣的一个。

sentences.zh: 我能问一下多米尼克吗，我们做过关于纳粹的系列节目，其中有人们穿着制服在夜间游行、火炬游行、为家庭举行活动，并将一种感伤的情绪与对犹太人的极端暴力结合起来等等。

sentences.en: at night and torchlit processions and holding things for families and combining a kind of schmaltzy sentimentality with extreme violence against Jews and so on.
sentences.zh: 如果美国存在一个法西斯政党，你认为三K党会是那个法西斯政党吗？

sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: And I think that's what makes the 1920s Klan the most interesting to me as a modern historian of the three.

sentences.en: Quite the reverse.

sentences.zh: 我认为三K党比意大利法西斯主义等组织更缺乏前瞻性。

sentences.en: The Klan is much less forward-looking, I think, than, for example, Italian fascism.
sentences.zh: 更倾向于向后看。

sentences.zh: 当然，三K党对战争毫无兴趣。

sentences.zh: 当然，三K党对战争毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: They just like riding around beating people up.

sentences.en: Yes.

sentences.en: But you're dead right.
sentences.zh: 但你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: There are some huge similarities.
sentences.zh: 两者确实有巨大的相似之处。

sentences.en: So victimhood, the family, hatred of the outsider, paramilitary violence, costumes, parades, rituals, torch-lit processions, aeroplanes.
sentences.zh: 比如受害者心态、家庭观念、对外来者的仇恨、准军事暴力、制服、游行、仪式、火炬游行、飞机等等。

sentences.en: Yeah, there are definite similarities.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实有明显的相似之处。

sentences.en: And for me, I would say there never has been a mass fascist movement in the United States.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，我认为美国从未有过大规模的法西斯运动。

sentences.en: But if you want to imagine what one might have looked like, I think it would look not unlike the 1920s Klan.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想想象它可能是什么样子，我认为它看起来和20世纪20年代的3K党没什么两样。

sentences.en: Not least because actually the people, just think about it demographically, the people who joined the 1920s Klan are not dissimilar
sentences.zh: 尤其是考虑到人口统计学上的事实，加入20世纪20年代3K党的人，与

sentences.en: from the people who joined the National Socialist Movement in 1920s, 1930s Germany.
sentences.zh: 加入20世纪20、30年代德国国家社会主义运动的人，并没有什么不同。

sentences.en: Protestant, small businessmen, salesmen, you know, people who feel threatened by, they don't like, they're not members of labor unions.
sentences.zh: 新教徒、小商人、推销员，你知道的，那些感到受到威胁、不喜欢某些事物、且不是工会成员的人。

sentences.en: They're not very rich.
sentences.zh: 他们不算太富有。

sentences.en: They're not very poor.
sentences.zh: 也不算太贫穷。

sentences.en: They feel squeezed.
sentences.zh: 他们感到被挤压。

sentences.en: They feel anxious about change.
sentences.zh: 他们对变革感到焦虑。

sentences.en: You know, they like dressing up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们喜欢穿上制服。

sentences.en: Do you think the fondness for kind of galloping around on horses is a legacy of the Wild West,
sentences.zh: 你认为那种喜欢骑着马四处奔跑的爱好，是美国西部荒野留下的遗产吗？

sentences.en: the sense of people on horses going out there and imposing law and order, whether there is no law
sentences.zh: 那种人们骑着马出去，在没有法律和秩序的地方强行实施法律和秩序的感觉，

sentences.en: and order, and that that's a hangover because the Wild West is being romanticized in films at the same time as the Ku Klux Klan are.
sentences.zh: 这是否是一种残留的影响？因为在电影中，西部荒野和3K党几乎是在同一时期被浪漫化的。

sentences.en: And it just becomes part of American mythology.
sentences.zh: 这已经成为了美国神话的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think American mythology absolutely has a cult of the vigilante.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为美国神话中绝对存在一种私刑崇拜。

sentences.en: Well, kind of Batman.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就像蝙蝠侠那样。

sentences.en: Yeah, look at Batman.
sentences.zh: 没错，看看蝙蝠侠。

sentences.en: The man who rides into town to, because the useless authorities can't do it to clean up the town.
sentences.zh: 那个骑马进城的人，因为无能的当局无法清理城市，所以他挺身而出。

sentences.en: And actually, you know, the reason it's so successful in, let's say, Indiana, is partly because Indiana had always had this tradition of vigilantes.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道，它之所以在印第安纳州等地如此成功，部分原因在于印第安纳州一直有这种私刑传统。

sentences.en: You know, it was not that long since Indiana had been on the frontier, a generation, a couple of generations.
sentences.zh: 要知道，印第安纳州脱离边疆状态并没有多久，也就一代人、两代人的时间。

sentences.en: So completely, yeah, that is not un-American.
sentences.zh: 所以完全正确，是的，这并非“非美国式”的。

sentences.en: It is very American.
sentences.zh: 这非常“美国”。

sentences.en: And that's why, yeah, exactly as you say, that's why Batman and stories of masked vigilantes are so popular.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么，正如你所说，蝙蝠侠和蒙面私刑者的故事会如此受欢迎。

sentences.en: You know, there's a comic book, I don't think you are a massive fan of comic books, by Alan Moore called Watchmen in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有一本漫画书，我想你不是漫画书的超级粉丝，是艾伦·摩尔在20世纪80年代创作的《守望者》。

sentences.en: Yeah, and they made it into a film.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们把它拍成了电影。

sentences.en: So there was then a TV series, which I have to say was brilliant, which departed from the comic book, but was all about the Klan and superheroes and vigilantes.
sentences.zh: 后来还有一部电视剧，我必须说非常精彩，它虽然背离了漫画原著，但主题全是关于3K党、超级英雄和私刑者。

sentences.en: And it basically played with the similarities between superheroes dressing up in masks and going out to enforce order and racist paramilitaries doing the same.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是在玩弄超级英雄戴着面具出去执法与种族主义准军事组织做同样事情之间的相似性。

sentences.en: And in fact, the Tulsa massacre of 1921 played a big part in that series.
sentences.zh: 事实上，1921年的塔尔萨大屠杀在那个系列剧中占了很大比重。

sentences.en: So yeah, I really recommend it actually.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，我真的很推荐它。

sentences.en: It didn't get the attention that it should have done, but it's a brilliant, brilliant series.
sentences.zh: 它没有得到应有的关注，但这是一部非常、非常精彩的剧集。

sentences.en: But anyway, that's enough of the Klan, Tom, because I think we should do something totally different next time, because that's the beauty of the rest of its history.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，关于3K党的话题就到此为止吧，汤姆，因为我觉得下次我们应该做点完全不同的内容，因为这就是《历史余韵》的魅力所在。

sentences.en: So tell us what you have lined up for next week.
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我们你下周准备了什么内容。

sentences.en: So we will be going to medieval Japan to explore the emergence of the samurai.
sentences.zh: 我们将前往中世纪的日本，探索武士的崛起。

sentences.en: And you say completely different, but of course, the samurai are people galloping around, indulging in acts of violence.
sentences.zh: 你说完全不同，但当然，武士也是一群骑马奔跑、沉溺于暴力行为的人。

sentences.en: And they're also incredibly mythologized.
sentences.zh: 而且他们也被极度神话化了。

sentences.en: So this is a series that will explore how the shogunate emerges and replaces the traditional imperial order.
sentences.zh: 所以这个系列将探讨幕府是如何崛起并取代传统的皇室秩序的。

sentences.en: But it is also a story that will feature flying heads and the ghosts of drowned samurai turning into crabs.
sentences.zh: 但这也会是一个充满飞头和溺死武士化作螃蟹的鬼魂的故事。

sentences.en: So that will be on its way next week.
sentences.zh: 所以下周就会推出。

sentences.zh: 当然，如果你是《历史余韵》俱乐部的成员，那么你周一就能收到全部四集关于武士的节目。

sentences.en: And to join them, you just go to therestishistory.com and sign up there.
sentences.zh: 要加入他们，只需访问 therestishistory.com 并注册即可。
